protocol.title: Purification of High Salinity Brine by Multi-Stage Ion Concentration Polarization Desalination
protocol.platform: PDMS-based microfluidic ICP (Ion Concentration Polarization) desalination device
protocol.objective: Multi-stage ICP electrical desalination of high-salinity brine (up to 100,000 ppm TDS) with trifurcated output strategy; simultaneous TDS and TSS removal; divalent cation characterisation; cost-competitive with MSF and MVR

membranes.type: Cation Exchange Membrane (CEM) only — unipolar conduction
membranes.anion_exchange_membrane: Fumasep FTCM-A (used in electrodialysis comparison experiments only)

electrodes.supplier: Fuel Cell Store, Inc., Boulder, CO
electrodes.reference_electrodes: Ag/AgCl (A-M Systems, WA); penetrate channels vertically to measure membrane voltage drop per cell only

plastic_scale_up_device.description: Plastic-based ICP/ED device assembled from CEMs, AEMs (ED only), carbon electrodes, and laser-cut plastic components

output_streams.concentrate: Top stream — ion-enriched; receives negatively charged suspended particles
output_streams.intermediate: Middle stream — concentration ~C0; majority fluid; re-fed to next ICP stage
output_streams.diluate: Bottom stream — ion-depleted; final treated water product

NaCl_brine.notes: Represents seawater, produced water, and high-salinity brine concentrate range

electrode_rinse.purpose: Exclude electrode/reaction overpotential from cell voltage measurement

fluorescent_tracers.fluid_tracing: Fluorescent color coding red dye (Kingscote Chemicals, Inc., OH), 1:1000 volumetric ratio
fluorescent_tracers.pH_indicator: pH indicator dye (Micro Essential Laboratory, Inc., NY), 5 wt%

bacterial_model.purpose: Visualise bacterial removal from diluate stream (Fig 7b)

oil_emulsion_model.tracer: Fluorescent color coding red dye, 1:1000 volumetric ratio
oil_emulsion_model.purpose: Visualise crude oil emulsion removal from diluate stream (Fig 7c)

demineralised_water.use: CEM pre-conditioning soak (minimum 48 h before experiments)

current_utilization_CU.description: Fraction of applied current used for salt removal in diluate flow; ideally unity in ED with no current loss
current_utilization_CU.notes: ICP with CEMs achieves CU > 1 due to diffusivity difference between Na+ and Cl- (DNa+ = 1.33e-9 m2/s, DCl- = 2.03e-9 m2/s)

energy_per_ion_removal_EPIR.description: Specific energy consumed per ion removed; proportional to voltage/CU
energy_per_ion_removal_EPIR.key_finding: EPIR linearly proportional to salt removal ratio regardless of current density, flow velocity, or membrane length (Fig 3c); optimal EPIR at minimum incremental salt removal ratio

multi_stage_strategy.description: Feed stream split into three output flows (concentrate/intermediate/diluate) by concentration distribution between CEMs. Intermediate stream at ~C0 is re-fed to next identical stage.
multi_stage_strategy.advantage_over_electrodialysis: Feed concentration kept constant at every stage; system always operates in economically favourable high-salinity EPIR regime; less inter-channel concentration difference and voltage drop

dilute_production_ratio_p.definition: Fraction of feed volume exiting as diluate output per stage
dilute_production_ratio_p.tradeoff: Lower p -> lower EPIR (energy) but higher stage number and capital cost; optimal p minimises total water cost ($/m3)

multi_stage_strategy.justification: 3 stages is representative optimised configuration for high-salinity range (SI-section 3.2.3); saltier feedwater requires more stages

operating_conditions.flow_driver: Negative pressure syringe pump (Harvard Apparatus PHD 2200)
operating_conditions.voltage_measurement: Keithley 236 source measurement unit; Ag/AgCl reference electrodes; Keithley 2000 Digital Multimeter
operating_conditions.cation_analysis: CCD-based ICP-AES instrument (ACTIVA-S, Horiba, Ltd., Japan)
operating_conditions.numerical_modelling: Coupled Poisson-Nernst-Planck-Navier-Stokes equations; finite volume method; Newton method and GMRES solver

steps.name: CEM membrane pre-conditioning
steps.notes: All Fumasep FTCM-E CEMs soaked in demineralised water (or process solution) for minimum 48 h at room temperature before experiments. BioScript: mix cem_membrane with demineralizedWaterPrep for 2880m.

steps.name: Brine feed dispense
steps.notes: Na2SO4 electrode rinse dispensed per-stage at point of use (rinse1, rinse2, rinse3) to avoid dead-code tokens in IR.

steps.name: Stage 1 — ICP desalination (first pass)
steps.operation: mix (ICP separation abstraction) + heat (electrical actuation abstraction)
steps.notes: Ion depletion zone forms adjacent to CEMs. Na+ and Cl- separated into concentrate (top) and diluate (bottom). Trifurcated: small diluate + majority intermediate (~C0) + small concentrate. heat at 25c abstracts timed constant-current actuation (no thermal processing in paper).

steps.name: Stage 2 — ICP desalination (second pass)
steps.notes: Intermediate stream re-fed at ~C0; feed concentration constant at every stage. System stays in high-salinity low-EPIR regime. No extensive feed concentration change unlike multi-stage electrodialysis.

steps.name: Stage 3 — ICP desalination (third pass)
steps.notes: Third and final ICP stage. Overall recovery fixed at 50% for cost comparison (SI-section 3.2.1). Diluate conductivity confirmed by flow-through probe; cation removal by ICP-AES (ACTIVA-S, Horiba).

steps.name: Salt removal QC detection
steps.detection_method: Flow-through conductivity probe (Microelectrode Inc.) + CCD-based ICP-AES (ACTIVA-S, Horiba)

steps.name: Suspended solids removal characterisation
steps.operation: mix (contaminant loading) + mix (ICP separation) + heat (electrical actuation)

contaminant_preparation.bacteria: E. coli K-12 MG1655 (GFP-expressing); 1.5 uM Alexa Fluor 488 for ICP zone visualisation
contaminant_preparation.oil_emulsion: Crude oil 1:50 in 0.1 M NaCl, sonicated 2 h; fluorescent red dye 1:1000

steps.mechanism: Negatively charged particles (negative zeta potential) migrate to concentrate stream (anode direction) via electrophoretic force en bloc; diluate exits particle-free
steps.notes: Majority of bio-contaminants (bacteria) and colloidal particles (oil emulsions) in nature carry negative zeta potentials; simultaneous TDS+TSS removal is a key ICP differentiator from conventional ED.

steps.name: Divalent cation removal characterisation
steps.result: Divalent cations removed proportionally or in excess of monovalent cations (SI-section 8); consistent with electrodialysis refs 41-43
steps.significance: Divalent cation removal prevents carbonate/sulfate precipitate formation in wellbore during produced water recycling

cost_analysis.ICP_water_cost_target: < $1/bbl for source water up to 70,000 mg/L TDS at 70% salt removal
cost_analysis.cost_dependence: Generally linear with feed water salinity

RO.notes: Not economically viable for brine; rapid power increase and recovery ratio decrease; pretreatment > $1/bbl

MSF.notes: Significant infrastructure and equipment; not competitive for partial desalination

MVR.notes: Currently used for produced water; high capital expense; complete desalination only

cost_analysis.ICP_advantage: Partial desalination (50-75%) sufficient for most applications (EOR, recycling); ICP cost (green zone, Fig 6) compares favourably over MSF and MVR
cost_analysis.capital_cost_basis: Sum of membrane/equipment expenses and maintenance cost dominated by membrane area (amount used)
cost_analysis.operating_cost_basis: Power consumption only (other minor costs neglected)

membrane_fouling_scaling.ICP_advantage: Operates without AEMs; pH shift and scaling occur near AEM not CEM; ICP voltage stable over extended operation vs electrodialysis (Fig 8d)
membrane_fouling_scaling.ED_comparison: ED voltage increases over time due to organic foulants in seawater; ICP voltage largely constant
membrane_fouling_scaling.CU_comparison: ED CU reduction ratio higher than ICP (Fig 8e); more fouling on ED membrane surface disrupts counter-ion transport
membrane_fouling_scaling.pH_observation: Significant pH changes near AEM in ED (acidification in diluate, basification in concentrate); not observed near CEM in ICP (Fig 8a/b)
membrane_fouling_scaling.test_conditions: Constant current density 500 A/m2; natural seawater feed (Revere Beach, MA); no prefiltration; 3 h duration

basic_blocks.label: main
basic_blocks.content: CEM conditioning, brine dispense, Stage 1-3 ICP separation, salt removal QC detect

bioscript_compiler_notes.ir_output: 10 basic blocks (BB1-BB10), 3 if/else gates, 12 CFG edges
bioscript_compiler_notes.duration_units: BioScript supports s and m only; h token not supported
bioscript_compiler_notes.heat_abstraction: heat at 25c abstracts timed constant-current electrical actuation; no thermal processing applied in paper; consistent with Samlali reference file convention
bioscript_compiler_notes.mix_abstraction: mix abstracts flow-through ICP separation event; not DMF electrode mixing
bioscript_compiler_notes.v1_fix: Removed dangling global rinseBuffer dispense (dead-code token in IR); Na2SO4 now dispensed per-stage at point of use only (rinse1, rinse2, rinse3, rinseDivalent)
